text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze said yesterday he disagrees with the Finance Ministry's view that Ft 4.6 billion should be allocated to subsidize church-run schools.
- Young Democrat house leader Jozsef Szajer has suggested a meeting of all parliamentary parties next Wednesday to discuss his party's defense charter proposal.

- Opposition members on the parliamentary commission investigating the Tocsik case intend to establish the responsibility of Prime Minister Gyula Horn and the cabinet in a final report on the case to be released soon.
- Pensions could rise 19% next year if wages go up 21.5%, in line with this year's forecasts.
- The opposition Democratic Forum said that his party will undertake to build 40,000 new homes in four years if it comes to power after next year's elections.
- Farmers' representatives announced a large-scale demonstration in Vas county on June 27 to protest against foreigners obtaining farmland through "pocket contracts."
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said EU accession negotiations due to begin next January could end by 2000, and all member states could ratify the admission of new members by 2002.
- An armed man opened fire on two Hungarian border guards, near Beremend, across from Croatia, Tuesday evening, but did not hit them.
- The World Bank is extending a $150 million loan toward the development of higher education in Hungary.
- Tourism revenues totalled $445 million in the first quarter, up 32% on the same period of 1996, while the expenditures were $286 million, an increase of 30%, the National Bank of Hungary reports.
- The National Association of Agricultural Cooperatives and Producers (MOSZ) will ask the state to guarantee wheat procurement prices of between Ft 20,000 and Ft 20,500 per ton next year.
- A total of Ft 2.7 billion is available for water system developments around and at Lake Balaton this year, of which Ft 1.3 billion is expected to be spent on sewage system.
- The president of Fotex yesterday hit back at Templeton Emerging Markets Fund, saying that a hostile takeover attempt lurks behind the fund's appeal to minority shareholders' rights.
- The Budapest Stock Exchange saw record prices and record volume yesterday, as the BUX hit a new record high of 6,480.41, after rising more than 167 points, or 2.65%.

- The State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.) announced that the consortium of New-York based Oil Capital Ltd. and the Chinese strategic investor MCC have won the tender for the ore mine Recski Ercbanyak Rt.

- The Eger-based electronic and robot component manufacturer Vilati Rt. has been awarded to the Hungarian consortium of MVA Vilati, Wallis and Hobal, the State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.) announced yesterday.
- Customs guards caught a Dutch citizen in possession of more than two kilograms of heroin on the Dacia express train at Lokoshaza border station Wednesday morning.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Finance Ministry is expected to propose a 0.4% cut in income taxes to 21.1% in 1998 from this year's 21.5% (23.1% in 1996).
- The State Money and Capital Markets Supervision (APTF) has withdrawn brokerage Csiky Ertekpapir's license to trade on the stock exchange.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) considers Hungary and Poland worthy of further investment, but calls for caution with the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
